findings.claim: The round 2 fix to the 'Request cookies are parsed leniently' decision made reads asymmetric with writes. Request values are now percent-decoded as UTF-8 (cookie-parser style) and their surrounding double quotes are removed, but the write path does not percent-encode: D-205 and the same decision make new Cookie(...), the setters and res.addCookie reject any value outside the RFC 6265 grammar. Express is symmetric because res.cookie encodes with encodeURIComponent, and NaruServe is not. Two results contradict the decision's own intent. (1) A value that is valid on the wire does not round-trip. The app sets new Cookie("x", "a%2Cb") ('%' is a legal cookie-octet), and on the next request req.cookie("x").getValue() returns "a,b". A quoted value "\"abc\"", which is legal per RFC 6265, comes back as abc. (2) The decision says only a request cookie 'with an invalid name or value' throws when echoed through res.addCookie(req.cookie("x")). With decoding, a fully valid browser cookie such as a%20b becomes "a b" once decoded, and echoing it now throws IllegalArgumentException. Code that never touched the value can turn into a 500.
findings.evidence: docs/research/naruserve-v1/waves/wave-5/design.md:114 (cookie decision: percent-decode on read, D-205 exception on new Cookie/setters/res.addCookie); design/00.design.md D-205; docs/api/cookie.md:43 (value row) and :78 (security: reject only, no encoding)
findings.suggested_fix: Make read and write symmetric. Option A, which is consistent with D-205's reject-not-encode rule and the Servlet model the Cookie class already follows: keep request values exactly as sent (no percent-decoding, no quote stripping) and still skip pairs with an invalid name. Then res.addCookie(req.cookie(x)) re-validates and throws only for values that really are invalid. Option B: keep decode-on-read and add encode-on-write in res.addCookie (encodeURIComponent for the value) instead of rejecting non-octet values. This needs D-205 narrowed to names and to CR/LF/';' in values, which is a frozen-item change, so Option A is preferred. Record the chosen rule and its round-trip guarantee in docs/api/cookie.md, and add a T34 round-trip case for a value containing '%'.
